title: Shield Proxy: policy runner and admin guardrail for API/runtime/console
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement a lightweight policy runner and enforcement proxy (Shield Proxy) that provides a consistent authorization layer across three planes: public API, internal runtime requests, and the Redwood Console. The proxy will evaluate RBAC v2 policies, inject audit metadata, and enforce admin guardrails (super-admin checks, emergency overrides, rate-limited destructive actions). This ticket covers design, PoC, integration with SSO/SAML SSO claims, audit log schema, and an initial canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Shield Proxy can evaluate and enforce RBAC v2 policies for API and runtime requests with <2ms median added latency in the fast path
Audit events emitted to our logging pipeline for every decision (allow/deny) with stable schema and trace IDs
Admin guardrail endpoints require explicit 2-step approval and emit high-fidelity audit records
SAML SSO-derived roles can be imported and mapped to RBAC v2 subjects during login flows
End-to-end integration tests covering happy path, deny path, and emergency override are passing in staging
migration_plan: Phase 1: deploy Shield Proxy as an opt-in sidecar for console UI services and internal runtime nodes in staging. Phase 2: run in parallel with legacy authorizer for 2 weeks while collecting metrics and audit diffs. Phase 3: flip enforcement for low-risk routes, expand to API gateway, then enable for high-risk admin routes. Provide rollback toggles and a flag to preserve legacy auth behavior per customer in Dedicated/Private deployments.
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy runner (policy predicates, condition evaluation, time-based rules)
Integration tests with local SAML idp (simulate role assertions and attribute mappings)
Load tests to quantify latency and tail percentiles under 10k req/s burst patterns
Chaos scenario: simulate policy evaluation backend timeout and verify graceful fallback policies (deny-by-default, cached allow when explicit)
open_questions: Do we store full policy evaluation traces in production or sample at 1% to limit sensitive data exposure?
Should emergency override require two-person approval for Dedicated/Private customers?
What is the canonical mapping format for SAML role attributes to RBAC subjects?
What retention window do compliance teams expect for decision-level audit events?
rollout_strategy: Canary first: small subset of Console traffic + dedicated staging runtime pods. Observe decision diffs vs legacy authorizer and audit event parity. After 7 days with no regression, increase traffic to 25%, then 75%. Finalize by enabling enforcement for admin routes only, holding non-admin routes in audit-only mode for an additional 14 days.
audit_strategy: Every authorization decision emits an audit row with fields: timestamp, actor_id, actor_source (sso|api-key|service), route, resource, action, policy_version, decision, reason_codes, trace_id, request_id, server_node. Audit rows are sent to the same immutable pipeline used by incident forensics and copied to a separate low-latency index for realtime console queries.
admin_controls: Role escalation approvals via Console with mandatory justification
Emergency mode toggle (requires ops-team consent and eight-hour auto-expiry)
Scoped API keys that bypass certain checks but leave a full audit trail
Granular RBAC policy editing permissions with preview-and-dry-run
saml_integration_notes: Support mapping from SAML 'eduPersonScopedAffiliation' and custom attributes into RBAC subject labels
IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows must both surface role assertions to short-lived session tokens
Implement a reconcile job that imports SAML group changes daily for Dedicated customers
Document canonical attribute names and provide a migration helper for customers with noisy SAML claims
observability: Expose per-route decision histograms in Console
Drilldown from audit event to trace span in distributed tracing system
